Write `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/persistence.test.mjs` (node:test): persistence, save failures, no-write rules and concurrency of a meeting-room booking server.

RULES: ES module, Node built-ins only (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`, fs/promises, path). Use the helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/server.mjs` (read it first: startServer({cwd, env}), request, postBooking, getBookings, writeStore, makeTmpDir, booking(overrides), delay, ROOT, JSON_TYPE). Do NOT edit helpers, server.mjs or public/. Extra helpers go in your test file. Exact equality on spec values (strictEqual/deepStrictEqual), never prefix/regex. Stop every server (finally/after) and rm tmp dirs. No console.log. File ≤ 450 lines, functions < 50 lines. Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2 && node --test test/persistence.test.mjs` until it passes. If a test fails on the real server and the spec below clearly says otherwise, do NOT weaken it: keep it and report it with repro.

Spec excerpt (full: /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/.team/notes/spec.md; backend notes .team/notes/api.md):
- After startup memory is the truth: outside changes to the file are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and never creates folders.
- Every change is saved before its reply: after a restart with the same DATA_FILE, bookings and the next id are as before.
- If saving fails (e.g. the data file's folder does not exist) the reply is 500 `{"error":"internal error"}` (Content-Type exactly `application/json; charset=utf-8`) and nothing changes, the next id included. The server keeps running.
- Concurrent requests behave as if handled one at a time: of several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and every other gets 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>`, and no id is given twice.
- Ids: first booking id 1, then next integer; never reused even after deletes and restarts. A booking is exactly {id, room, title, date, start, end}.
- Overlap = same room, same date, each starts before the other ends.
- Data layout: `{"nextId":N,"bookings":[...]}`.

Tests:
1. Saved before reply: right after a POST's 201 arrives, read+parse DATA_FILE → contains the booking and nextId 2; right after DELETE 204 → booking gone, nextId still 2.
2. Restart: POST 3 bookings (ids 1,2,3), DELETE 3, DELETE 1, stop, start again with same DATA_FILE → GET deepStrictEqual [booking 2]; POST → id 4. DELETE 4, restart, POST → id 5. Also: create 1,2; delete 2; create → 3 (no reuse in one run).
3. Outside changes ignored: after start (seeded with 1 booking, nextId 2), overwrite the file with 'garbage' → GET still returns the seeded booking; POST → 201 id 2; file now parses to nextId 3 with both bookings. Also overwrite with a different valid store (nextId 50) → next POST still uses the in-memory id.
4. No writes: seed a valid store written pretty-printed (JSON.stringify(s,null,2)) so its bytes are distinctive; record bytes and mtimeMs; start; send GET /, GET /app.js, GET /api/rooms, GET /api/bookings, GET /api/bookings?date=2026-11-03, GET /api/bookings?date=bad, GET /nope, PUT /api/bookings, DELETE /api/bookings/99, DELETE /api/bookings/abc, DELETE /api/bookings/1/ , POST invalid JSON (400), POST wrong content type (415), POST 10001-byte body (413), POST overlapping the seeded booking (409); then delay(100); bytes identical and mtimeMs unchanged. Then a successful POST changes the file.
5. Save failure on POST: DATA_FILE=tmp/d/b.json with tmp/d missing → POST valid → status 500, body deepStrictEqual {error:'internal error'}, content-type exact; GET → []; tmp/d does not exist; stdout still exactly one listening line (handle.stdout()). Then mkdir tmp/d, POST → 201 with id 1 (next id unchanged), file written.
6. Save failure on DELETE: seed tmp/d/b.json (booking id 1, nextId 2), start, rename tmp/d → tmp/d2; DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 500 internal error; GET still shows booking 1; POST another → 500; rename back; POST → 201 id 2; DELETE 1 → 204; file reflects it.
7. Keeps running: after several 500s, GET /api/rooms still 200, server process still alive.
8. Concurrency overlapping: 12 POSTs at once (Promise.all) for Aurora 2026-11-03 with varied overlapping times (09:00-10:00, 09:30-10:30, 08:30-09:30, 09:15-09:45, ...) → exactly one 201; each other is 409 with body deepStrictEqual {error:`room is already booked from ${winner.start} to ${winner.end}`}; GET has exactly that 1 booking with id 1; file has 1 booking, nextId 2.
9. Concurrency distinct: 15 non-overlapping POSTs at once (rooms × dates × times) → all 201, ids sorted deepStrictEqual [1..15]; file has 15 bookings, nextId 16.
10. Concurrent DELETE of the same id twice → one 204 and one 404 {error:'booking not found'}. Concurrent POSTs while saving fails (missing folder) → all 500; then mkdir; POST → id 1.

Final message: test count, pass/fail, any failing-on-real-code test with repro, line count.

# API / server notes — backend — 2026-11-02

Implements spec.md sections Server, API, Booking rules and Page bullet 1 in `server.mjs` (one file, built-ins only).

## Data file layout (DATA_FILE, default `bookings.json`, resolved against cwd)
```json
{"nextId": 3, "bookings": [{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}]}
```
- Written compactly (`JSON.stringify`, no trailing newline) with a plain `writeFile`, only after a successful POST or DELETE.
- Bookings are kept in insertion order in the file. The API sorts them on GET.
- Startup accepts only exactly this layout (see decisions.md): the top level has exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`; every booking has exactly the 6 keys with valid values; ids are unique, at least 1 and below `nextId`; no two bookings overlap. Anything else, including an empty file, bad JSON or a folder, prints `cannot read data file <DATA_FILE as given>` and exits 1. ENOENT (missing file or folder) means start empty with `nextId` 1.
- To seed a test, write a valid file like the one above before starting the server.

## Starting it in tests
- Run `spawn(process.execPath, [<abs path to server.mjs>], { cwd: <tmp dir>, env: { ...process.env, PORT: '0', DATA_FILE: <path> } })`.
- Wait for stdout to match `/^listening on http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:(\d+)\n$/` and take the port from it. stdout carries only that line.
- Startup failures write one line to stderr and exit with code 1, without printing on stdout:
  - Bad PORT (not all digits, or above 65535): `invalid PORT "<value>"`.
  - Port already in use: `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>: EADDRINUSE`.
- Kill the child process with `child.kill()` when done. There is no graceful-shutdown handler.
- To make a save fail, point DATA_FILE into a folder that does not exist, for example `<tmp>/missing/b.json`. Startup works (ENOENT), but every POST or DELETE that would change data replies 500 `internal error` and nothing changes.
- The page files are read on every request from `<folder of server.mjs>/public/` (`index.html`, `app.js`). If one is missing, that request gets 500 `internal error` as JSON, and the API keeps working.

## Behaviour details testers may care about
- The body is always read in full (all of it is counted, only the first 10000+ bytes are kept), and the reply is sent after it ends. Rule order is 415, 413, 400 (object, room, title, date, start, end, order), then 409.
- Overlap checks, saving and the in-memory change all run inside one promise queue, so concurrent overlapping POSTs give one 201 and the rest 409.
- DELETE `<id>` must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and is compared to `String(booking.id)`.
- 405 replies have no `Allow` header. HEAD and OPTIONS get 405 on known paths.
- The scratch smoke script `.team/scratch/smoke.mjs` (backend, not shipped) covers about 55 cases. Testing may copy ideas from it.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.
